source.title: A Riemannian mean field formulation for two-layer neural networks with batch normalization

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling materially affects the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper numerically illustrates training dynamics of two-layer batch-normalized networks and compares them with vanilla networks, but does not test whether benchmark classification training reaches near-zero error.
record.gate_note: The paper's own numerical results concern neuron direction and speed in Figures 1–3. It provides no training classification error or benchmark result. Claims about BN speeding learning and reducing learning-rate sensitivity are discussed, but no measured benchmark accuracy or error is reported.
record.test_reason: The study derives population-BN parameter dynamics and illustrates neuron-direction speeds, rather than measuring accuracy gains, training-loss convergence speed, or tolerated learning rates against a non-BN control. These related outcomes do not test V6. Its conditional infinite-width global-optimality theorem does not test the architectures, outcomes, or width comparison in V1–V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify population BN with a change of parameter-space metric, derive a Wasserstein gradient flow for the infinite-width model, establish existence, and prove global optimality conditional on convergence and additional assumptions. They discuss potential training benefits through neuron-direction dynamics; they do not establish unconditional convergence or measured accuracy and learning-rate advantages.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies gradient-flow dynamics of two-layer population-BN models and their infinite-width mean-field formulation, rather than benchmark classification training with the methods and measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The numerical illustrations vary BN versus non-BN and neuron initialization magnitude; the paper also discusses dependence on data covariance and neuron magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.1 and Figure 1 compare neuron-direction dynamics with and without BN under anisotropic input covariance, diag(5,1). BN changes direction-dependent speeds and the concentration of neurons along significant data directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Population BN changes neuron-direction dynamics according to alignment with input covariance in the illustrated two-layer model.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.2 and Figure 2 show faster direction convergence for neurons initialized with smaller magnitudes; the larger initialization is ten times the smaller one.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron initialization magnitude controls direction-learning speed in the illustrated population-BN model.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.3 and Figure 3 describe small neurons increasing in magnitude after the first discrete gradient step. No learning-rate sweep or comparison of tolerated rates is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Population BN produces first-step magnitude amplification for small neurons under discrete gradient descent.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 5 establishes global optimality of the infinite-width population-BN flow's limit, conditional on Wasserstein convergence, technical regularity assumptions, and an initial-support separation condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, a convergent infinite-width population-BN gradient flow has a globally minimizing limit.

record.problems: The numerical evidence relevant to training behavior is illustrative and qualitative, with no reported error bars or benchmark classification outcomes. The convergence result is theoretical and conditional on the stated assumptions and convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No rows qualify: the figure descriptions concern speed and neuron directions, not training classification error or accuracy; cited prior studies are not results of this paper.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size, stopping, or regularization conditions.
Spurious-minimum frequency in ReLU teacher-student problems and its reduction with one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and deep-network training with special initialization or Fixup.
Activation-matched or orthogonal initialization effects on network learning speed and trainable depth. Different neuron magnitudes are compared only through direction dynamics.
Loss recovery, curvature evolution, and divergence relative to the initial linearized stability threshold.
Whether BN increases accuracy faster or permits higher learning rates than the same network without BN; whether Fixup matches normalized residual-network training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6 and V6 from tested_not_extracted to not tested. The illustrative results are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including with corrupted or random labels, and the stated size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Whether extra student width reduces spurious minima in teacher-student ReLU problems.
Whether depth degrades training error in plain convolutional networks, whether identity shortcuts prevent it, and whether special initialization or Fixup trains very deep networks.
Whether activation-matched, orthogonal, or convolutional initializations change training speed or trainable depth.
Whether training recovers from learning rates above stability limits, curvature behavior, and divergence under full-batch training.

The paper compares BN and non-BN two-layer models in numerical illustrations and discusses training speed and learning-rate adaptivity, but does not report a quantified accuracy-gain or learning-rate-tolerance outcome of the kind stated in V6.
